Guide Cosmoctopus through the Inky Realm, a flexible configuration of tiles, to gather resources and obtain powerful cards that represent relics, scripture, hallucinations and constellations. Harness the power of these bizarre objects and experiences, craft potent card combinations and be the first to gain 8 tentacles to win! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Cards 4 Game End 5 Private Investigator (Co-Op Mode) Overview Gain 8 Tentacles and summon the Cosmoctopus first! Turn On your turn, move the Cosmoctopus, optionally play a card, discard down to 8 cards, then direct the Cosmoctopus towards the next player First, move the Cosmoctopus orthogonally and gain the bonus of the space it lands on. Additionally, you MAY spend any resource of your choice to move it one space more for each resource spent, only the final landing space will generate rewards though After which, pick a card from your hand to play if desired, this may result in further cards being played via previous card effects, but usually you can only play 1 card. To play a card you must be able to afford it, most cards show in the top left banner a specific amount of one resource type plus a specific amount of any combination of resources required to pay. You have the option to discard cards from your hand, these then count as resources of the same type, e.g. red cards discard for the red resource. Make sure you have no more than 8 Cards and 8 of each unique resource at end of turn, discarding the excess If at any point you are unlucky enough to have 13 of a resource and the Forbidden Knowledge of that resource is still available, discard them all and gain two Tentacles along with the matching Forbidden Knowledge of that resource. Resource discounts apply to this, except for wildcards (unless they specifically say so). When you gain your first Tentacle, you can take a First Contact card of your choosing from those still available Cards Scriptures These give you a permanent resource to continuously use, however they cannot be used for the Wild cost unless it is a Permanent Wild resource. If the Scripture has the Submerge icon, discard Scriptures and Relics from the Market and move the Cosmoctopus once for each card discarded this way, resolve the effect of EACH space entered in this way. Relics These give you a permanent ability going forward, also if it contains the Devotee symbol then once only you draw a card from the Devotee deck Hallucinations These give one off effects then are discarded, if the purple lightning bolt is shown you can play a second card if you can afford to Constellations These do nothing when played, and have no ongoing effect, instead when you gain resources rather than taking them into your supply you can choose to add to an active Constellation. You always start from the top left, then follow the arrows to see what resource the Constellation desires next. Once all spaces are filled, the effect resolves and the resources and the card are discarded. Note: You have to fill it at the moment resources are gained, resources already in your supply CANNOT be used to complete a Constellation. Game End The game ends as soon as a player has 8 Tentacles, they win! Private Investigator (Co-Op Mode) The PI can be used to turn this into a co-operative game. The players are trying to ALL gain 8 Tentacles before the PI. Each PI card that can be used will occupy but not block a certain type of resource space. If you move onto an Investigated space, the PI also gains the depicted resource. If you move through an Investigated space to finish your movement on a different location, the PI does NOT gain anything. The PI also has special effects when they gain a Tentacle, gain a Forbidden Knowledge, and they reveal a permanent effect when they gain their 5th Tentacle. [Rating: 2/10] Atrociously overstayed it's welcome at 4. Swore we did something wrong with the rules but we were playing it correctly. Runs away too long without enough mitigation on the market row. Constellation cards take waaaay to long to fulfill without enough other ways to get tentacles. One of the worst games I've played in a long time.

[Rating: 2/10] Production is awesome. Well done on the graphics and the curious font choices giving me more "world immersion".  This game is so undeniably slow. It's  tedious resource gathering back and forth. And the main way to accelerate the game is hamstrung by needing to complete 8 tentacles first by mostly playing really expensive quests with unintuitive sequencing.   Turn order never changed. It never really got easier, just more annoying, and while production is cute and effective, the resource gathering and card play restrictions ... just break every fun strategic vision arc I could get with this ga

[Rating: 3/10] Snooooore.  This is aesthetically fantastic, but mechanically dull.  Main actions are way too tedious, and the cost/reward ratio feels skewed towards simplicity for no real purpose. This wants to be a worker placement game, except it kind of became worker movement without any of the things that make worker movement actually interesting e.g. Yokohama. I just don't understand why the main actions are blander than soggy weetbix.   Cards in contrast to the above feel overdesigned. The gap between the cards being interesting and exciting to use and then realising you're about 6 turns of boring main

[Rating: 3/10] An engine building game where players move around in a 3x3 grid, trigger action on that spot (gain resources and/or cards), and play cards for points/powers/actions. Once a player gains 8 octopus tentacles, they win.

[Rating: 3/10] Overly long for it is, quite random, light and straightforward engine building game. If this would take like 30 minutes it would be fine but even 60 minutes is painfully long for this game, and if it takes 90 minutes or more then it is just torture. Why? It is just that simple and repetitive.   It takes too long to setup an engine in this game and in the meantime you should deny every possible constellation card you can from your opponents. [Rating: 3/10] very clumsy mechanics. resource gathering is slow and uninteresting, same goes to octopus movements and playing effective cards. also if your opponent has 3-4 tentacles more there's normally no reason to go further as the winner is obvious. we had this problem every other game and there's no way to catch-up. sad because the theme and the design are great!

[Rating: 3/10] Just sort of 'bleh'. Hard to spend time on 'bleh' when so much 'non-bleh' exists.

[Rating: 3/10] Once players realise the importance of rushing to get the forbidden knowledge the game becomes stale and boring. The illusion of choice is dispelled and the inevitably of defeat once someone gains a lead early on turns the game into a disappointing overlong grind.

[Rating: 3/10] Gross. Too long, boring repetitive action selection, no catch up mechanism, so many weird tiny icons, little opportunity to plan ahead, swingy combos. Not for me.
